Overview

API Development & Integration at AtherIQ

Integration work goes wrong in predictable ways: an undocumented endpoint changes, an authentication token expires with nothing watching, a retry storm takes down a partner's service, or nobody can say what a field means because the contract only ever existed in a developer's head.

We treat the API as a product with a specification, versioning, authentication, rate limiting and documentation — whether it is an interface you are publishing to partners or one you are consuming from a third party.

For inbound integration work we handle the parts that are easy to skip and expensive to skip: idempotency, retry policy, error handling, credential rotation and monitoring that tells you an integration is failing before your customers do.

Talk it through first

Bring the problem rather than a specification. We will tell you what the work involves, where the risk sits and roughly what it costs before you commit to anything.

What we provide

Included in This Service

The concrete deliverables. Where something is out of scope for your budget, we say so before the quotation rather than after.

REST API design & development

Resource modelling, versioning strategy, pagination, filtering and consistent error contracts, documented with OpenAPI.

Third-party API integration

Payment gateways, shipping and logistics providers, messaging and email services, accounting platforms and government or banking portals.

Authentication & authorisation

OAuth 2.0, JWT, API keys and mutual TLS, with credentials held server-side and rotated on a defined schedule.

Webhooks & event handling

Signed inbound webhooks with replay protection, plus outbound event delivery with retries and dead-letter queues.

API gateway & rate limiting

Throttling, quotas, caching and routing through Azure API Management or AWS API Gateway.

Monitoring & documentation

Health checks, latency and error-rate alerting, structured logging, and reference documentation your team can actually use.

Business benefits

Why It Matters Commercially

Outcomes rather than a restatement of the feature list.

Integrations that fail loudly

Monitoring and alerting mean a broken connection is a notification, not a customer complaint three days later.

Safe to change

Versioned contracts let you evolve an API without breaking every consumer that depends on it.

Faster onboarding

Documented endpoints and predictable conventions cut the time any new developer or partner needs to integrate.

Credentials stay protected

Keys and secrets live in server-side configuration and secret stores, never in front-end code or repositories.

Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you integrate third-party APIs into our application?

Yes. We integrate payment, shipping, communication, accounting, mapping and industry-specific APIs, including handling authentication, retries and the error cases most integrations skip.

Can you build an API for our existing system?

Yes. We commonly put a documented, secured API layer in front of a legacy application or database so newer systems can consume its data without depending on its internals.

How do you keep API keys and secrets secure?

Secrets are stored in a managed secret store such as Azure Key Vault or AWS Secrets Manager, injected as configuration at runtime, never committed to source control and never exposed to the browser.

What happens if a third-party service goes down?

We design for it: timeouts, exponential backoff, circuit breakers and queued retries, so a partner outage degrades one feature rather than taking your application with it.

Ready to scope it?

Send us what you have — a brief, a wireframe, a spreadsheet of the current process, or just a description of what is not working.
